1#main: Places obligated in mezuzah. In it are 23 seifim. These are the places obligated in mezuzah: gates of houses and gates of courtyards of countries and towns, cattle sheds, attics, and storehouses of wine and oil, and a woman's house, and a partners' house—all are obligated. {Rama: And specifically when the partners' house is of Israelites; but a house of an Israelite and a non-Jew is exempt from mezuzah (Mordechai, first chapter of Avodah Zarah). And likewise courtyards or towns where some non-Jews live are exempt from mezuzah (Chidushei Agudah, first chapter of Yoma).}
2#main: A straw house, a wood house, and a cattle house are obligated; and if women bathe in them, since they stand there naked, it is not fitting for the Divine Presence to be there—no mezuzah. {Rama: And specifically these; but an actual room—even a place where a man and woman sleep and engage in relations—is obligated in mezuzah (in a responsum of Maharil, and so Beit Yosef). And some are lenient and say that wherever women lie, it is exempt from mezuzah (Beit Yosef in the of Semak and Kol Bo and Mordechai end of Hilchos Mezuzah). And it appears to me that where the door is from inside and when they lie there they close the door and the mezuzah is outside, it is obligated according to all (own reasoning in Darkei Moshe, and so in responsum of Maharil siman 98).}
3#main: In a synagogue, if there is a dwelling for any person, it is obligated in mezuzah. {Rama: And if there is a dwelling in the courtyard before the synagogue, the courtyard is obligated and the synagogue is exempt (Beit Yosef in the name of Rabbenu Yerucham).}
4#main: A privy, a bathhouse, a tannery, and a mikveh are exempt, because they are not made for dignified dwelling.
5#main: In a place where there is filth, such as where infants are commonly found—it is good to cover the mezuzah; and in a clean place, it is good that it be visible.
6#main: A portico—that is, a place that has three walls and a ceiling—even if it has two doorposts in the fourth direction, it is exempt, because the doorposts are to support the ceiling and not for mezuzot (words of the Rambam, chapter 6 of Hilchos Sefer Torah, halachah 3). But if it has a partition also in the fourth direction, even if it is low, or if it is made of windows upon windows, it is obligated.
7#main: A balcony that is a way to ascend to upper rooms, and a gatehouse and a watchman's booth are exempt; and if a house is open to one of these, they are obligated. And some say a gatehouse is obligated even if no house is open to it (Tur and poskim in the name of R' Yitzchak).
8#main: A gatehouse open to a house and to a courtyard is obligated in two mezuzot—one where it opens to the house and one where it opens to the courtyard.
9#main: A gatehouse standing between the watchman's booth and the house is obligated in two mezuzot—one where it opens to the house and one where it opens to the booth.
10#main: A study hall is exempt from mezuzah; and if it has a doorway through which one regularly goes out to his house, that doorway is obligated in mezuzah. And some say a study hall is obligated in mezuzah, and it is proper to be concerned for their words—but one does not recite a blessing on it.
11#main: A sukkah on Sukkot, a house on a ship, and shops in markets are exempt.
12#main: Two booths of potters, one inside the other—the inner one is obligated and the outer one exempt.
13#main: A house that does not have four by four amot is exempt; and if it has enough to square four by four amot equally—even if its length exceeds its width, or it is round, or has five corners—it is obligated (Rambam there, halachah 2).
14#main: A house that has no ceiling is exempt. If part of it was roofed and part not—if the roofing was opposite the doorway, it is obligated in mezuzah, provided there be four by four in the roofed part.
15#main: A house, even if it has no doors, is obligated in mezuzah; and some exempt it.
16#main: Many rooms one inside another—all are obligated in mezuzah.
17#main: If a house has many doorways open to a courtyard or to the public domain, and all were made for entry and exit of the household members—all are obligated, even if the dwellings were reduced and they are not now accustomed to go out and come in except through one of them.
18#main: A house that has many doorways—even if one is not accustomed to go out and come in except through one of them, one must make a mezuzah on every doorway. {Rama: Since they were made for entry and exit (implied in the Tur). A cellar that has a doorway from the street where they bring in wine in large barrels, and has a small doorway from the house through which they always enter and exit—if the small doorway is fit for a mezuzah, it is obligated and the large one exempt; and if the small one is not fit for a mezuzah, the large one is obligated and the small one exempt (Beit Yosef in the name of an Ashkenazic responsum, and it is in the writings of Maharil siman 99).}
19#main: An opening between a house and an attic, and they ascend to it by a ladder and make around the ladder an enclosure of partitions sometimes below at the feet of the ladder and sometimes above at its head, and it has the form of a doorway where they make it—it is obligated; and if they made it above and also below, it is obligated in two.
20#main: A doorway behind the door—if it has doorposts a tefach high, it is obligated in mezuzah.
21#main: One doorway divided by a pillar in the middle—wherever there is recognizable hinge on this side and that side toward the pillar, they are like two doorways and require a mezuzah for each doorway; but wherever there are no hinges toward the pillar, the pillar does not divide it into two, for it is only for decoration.
22#main: One who rents a house outside Eretz Yisrael and dwells in an inn in Eretz Yisrael is exempt from mezuzah for thirty days; and one who rents a house in Eretz Yisrael is obligated in mezuzah immediately because of settling Eretz Yisrael. (And the same law applies to one who borrows a house—like a renter) (Beit Yosef in the name of R' Rabbenu Menachem, and so in the Gemara).
23#main: One who rents a house from a non-Jew is obligated in mezuzah.
